commit_reviews.summary: Clean greenfield scaffolding that sets up ts-jest test infra and a dependency set (commander, gray-matter, marked) well-matched to a CLI static site generator.

problems: default page/index markup duplicated between templates.ts and generator.ts (two sources of truth)
two-step init() lifecycle instead of constructor injection
template/layout frontmatter fields ignored in non-engine path
commit_reviews.summary: Additive, backward-compatible Handlebars templating with a dedicated `TemplateEngine` module and optional `--templates` CLI flag, cleanly wired through build/generator/parser.

problems: timer inflation up to 30s risks masking true regressions
polling retry loop is a workaround rather than a root-cause fix
commit_reviews.summary: Coherent test-stability commit that disables parallel Jest workers, swaps polling for awaitWriteFinish, closes WS clients before the server, and extends timeouts.

compounding_issues: Session 1 committed node_modules/ and dist/ (~5,248 files, ~978K lines) with no .gitignore, permanently bloating every later commit and polluting AST/convention analysis
The story run truncated after Session 3 (integration) — the planned Session 4 refactor and Session 5 incremental-builds sessions never executed, so the full 5-session arc was not realized

Session 3's live-reload feature was over-scoped, hit the 900s timeout, and required a continuation commit (maxWorkers:1, awaitWriteFinish, WS teardown reorder, inflated timers) to stabilize flaky tests
generator.ts retains a parallel non-template HTML fallback path even after the TemplateEngine was integrated, duplicating rendering logic and creating two sources of truth
Templates module uses a two-step init() lifecycle instead of constructor injection, and default page/index markup is duplicated between templates.ts and generator.ts
key_decisions: Clean module decomposition (parser, generator, templates, build, serve, types) with an optional TemplateEngine injected into generator functions
Handlebars template engine with layouts, partials, and per-page frontmatter template selection, wired through build/generator
Optional --templates CLI flag so the build stays functional without templates, falling back to default HTML generation
Chokidar watcher + ws WebSocket live-reload server with debounced rebuilds, awaitWriteFinish stability handling, and a path-traversal guard (403) in the dev server
Jest config pinned to maxWorkers:1 with extended timeouts in the continuation commit to fix test flakiness
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily but the run was cut short. Session 1 laid a coherent greenfield architecture (parser/generator/build/types) with a thorough test suite, though it committed dependency bloat that haunted every later commit. Session 2 was the cleanest step: a 154-line Handlebars template engine with layouts and partials covered by 384 lines of tests. Session 3 added a well-designed live-reload server (chokidar + ws, debounced rebuilds, path-traversal guard) but over-reached, timing out at 900s; the continuation commit then demonstrated genuine debugging by tightening the watcher config and test timing to stabilize the suite. The visible arc improves feature-by-feature and ends on a stabilizing bug-fix, but the sequence terminates at Session 3, missing the refactor and cross-cutting phases that would have shown how the architecture compounds.
story_review.summary: A logically progressive, well-architected build for the three sessions it completed, undermined by Session 1's committed dependency bloat and an over-scoped Session 3 that required a continuation commit, with the run ending before the planned refactor and caching sessions.
